origins.section: A Quality Gate Runs Every Rule After the Schema and Before the Model
Rules Across Projects Catch Errors No Single Field Shows
Severity Follows What a Finding Proves: Errors Block, Warnings Report

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-gate-order: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-gate-order: 12.2.2: "every snapshot it accepts has every field typed and every id resolved, so the model can be built. That is not the same as a model worth solving." The service order is "the schema (can the model be built?), the gate (is the data worth solving?), then the model."
recorded.prompt:q-quiet-cycle: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-quiet-cycle: "The solver does not say "infeasible". Neither project is must-do, so the plan that funds neither satisfies every row, and the solver returns it". The output shows "cycle  plan funds P015: False, P016: False" and "solver: OPTIMAL", described as "with nothing in the result to say so".
recorded.prompt:q-severity: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-severity: "Why is drift a warning and not an error...? Because a large change is not proof of a wrong one. A new regulatory program can triple a year's budget. The drift rule cannot tell a tripling from a typo, so it reports and lets the sound rules decide whether to block."

recorded.prompt:q-gate-order: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.outcome:q-gate-order: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'c'
recorded.because:q-gate-order: All four options share the same 'That X, though Y' hedged frame, are about the same length, and none repeats stem words or uses absolutes in a way that gives it away; picking one needs knowing what a schema check proves.

gates.says: all 9 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-gate-order:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-gate-order:a: "P023 must-do, its lag typed 3      schema: valid   solver: INFEASIBLE". A snapshot that passes the schema can still have no plan.
recorded.prompt:q-gate-order:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-gate-order:b: In the parent-cycle case the schema is valid and the result is "an `OPTIMAL` plan that has lost a project because of a typo in a link", so the plan is not right.
recorded.prompt:q-gate-order:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-gate-order:d: Passing the schema establishes that "the model can be built". The gate's rules are "Rules Across Projects" that "the schema accepts", not repeats of the schema's checks.
recorded.prompt:q-quiet-cycle:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-quiet-cycle:b: "The solver does not say "infeasible"." The printed status is OPTIMAL.
recorded.prompt:q-quiet-cycle:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-quiet-cycle:c: "cycle  plan funds P015: False, P016: False".
recorded.prompt:q-quiet-cycle:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-quiet-cycle:d: The output shows "schema: valid   solver: OPTIMAL, NPV $22,637k". The model was built and solved without an error.
recorded.prompt:q-severity:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-severity:a: "a large change is not proof of a wrong one. A new regulatory program can triple a year's budget."
recorded.prompt:q-severity:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-severity:b: When the budgets grew fivefold, "the solve would run, and the drift warnings would sit in the report beside a plan that a planner can check". A warning does not block, and the page treats that plan as one a planner can check.
recorded.prompt:q-severity:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-severity:c: "On a snapshot where every budget grew fivefold, no sound rule would fire: the solve would run". Nothing guarantees a refusal, and the page's reason is that the rule cannot tell a real change from a typo, not that the solver would refuse.
